author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her talk “Girl Math, Boy Logic, the Truth about Human Spending,” tax professional Temiloluwa Olubakinde explores the viral concept of “Girl Math” to reveal how emotional logic drives all human financial behavior. Deconstructing both "Girl Math" and its counterpart, "Boy Logic," she breaks down the psychological triggers — like mental accounting and loss aversion — that we use to justify spending. Ultimately, Temi argues that using humor to laugh at our financial quirks removes shame, fosters empathy, and serves as an unexpected gateway to truer financial literacy.

I am a tax professional who loves exploring why people make their choices, especially when it comes to money. My experience working in tax and accounting showed me how emotion drives even the most logical financial decisions. Outside of work, I focus on simplifying complex money topics for young adults and communities who often feel excluded from financial conversations. Through projects like writing, podcasting, and pub
title: The truth behind our money spending habits | Temiloluwa Olubakinde | TEDxTAMU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if play isn’t something we do when the serious work is over, but one of the ways we get better at it?

Take a piece of paper. Draw yourself as a superhero. You have twenty seconds. For those few moments, you were playing with possibilities. Then, without noticing, you started performing. In this thought-provoking TEDxKMCT talk, Dr. Manu Melwin Joy invites us to recognise this shift and question what we lose when we grow up and learn to stay within the blueprint.

Dr. Manu takes us into a training room filled with angry employees, where his carefully planned session fell apart. When the participants refused to follow his plan, he improvised a game: express real workplace issues, but only through movie dialogues. It didn’t solve everything, but it changed how people could communicate.

That experience changed how he viewed play. Not as an escape or something childish, but as the willingness to experiment, imagine, and try, even if it means failing. He explores three ways play can t
title: The Serious Power of Play | Manu Melwin Joy | TEDxKMCT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the thing you thought was standing in your way was never the real obstacle?

Anaida Stanly was born with a fracture in her right hand and was later diagnosed with Osteogenesis Imperfecta, commonly known as Brittle Bone Disease. She has lived through more than 40 fractures and four surgeries. With metal rods inside her body, she jokingly calls herself the “Steel Lady.” Behind this humorous title lies a childhood shaped by hospitals, treatment rooms and recovery. In this honest and uplifting TEDxKMCT talk, she captures her journey in one sentence: “I have breakable bones, but an unbreakable spirit.”

Anaida takes us through the moments that shaped her life. She started school only in the first standard, and when she struggled to see the board, her parents wondered whether she had a learning disability. However, her full marks in every subject proved that the difficulty was never her ability to learn. She recalls schools that refused to admit her and how her mother’s one-year con
title: Breakable Bones with Unbreakable Spirit | Anaida Stanly | TEDxKMCT

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if our greatest inheritance isn't money, property or possessions, but something far more valuable that often goes unnoticed? From unspoken family lessons to generations of wisdom, we inherit experiences we never lived and lessons we never personally learned. This invisible inheritance shapes not just individuals and families but entire nations. This talk explores the wisdom we overlook, the experiences we inherit, and the choices we make about what to preserve, question, and pass forward. Shreya Dafria is a Grade 12 student and deputy head girl of Daly College, Indore, and a recipient of the Sanghi Trophy and Dewas Cup for Best All-Round Student. She scored 99% in her Class X CBSE Board examinations and has won national-level accolades in fine arts, debating, and Model United Nations. A competitive shooter, she has qualified for international trials and represented her state at the National Shooting Championships for three consecutive years. As Chairperson and Deputy Secretary-Ge
title: The inheritance we never claim !! | Shreya Dafria | TEDxDaly College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Naavya Seksaria is a Grade XI student at Daly College, Indore, with a keen interest in economics, which she hopes to pursue at university. Having secured 9 A*s in her IGCSE examinations, she has explored economic questions through independent research papers. An avid debater and Model United Nations enthusiast, she has served on the Executive Boards of multiple conferences and is the student editor of The Daly Prophet, her school's student newspaper. Fluent in multiple languages, she is drawn to questions that challenge conventional perspectives and examine the forces shaping individual choices and opportunities.

Originally inspired by the economic concept of opportunity cost, Naavya's talk, Decoding How Much of Me Is Actually Me?, takes a deeper look at the circumstances underlying the choices we make. While economics often examines the trade-offs involved in individual decisions, she questions something more fundamental: how much of our ability to choose is itself determined by cir
title: Decoding How Much of Me Is Actually Me | Naavya Seksaria | TEDxDaly College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What do we really inherit? Is it wealth and possessions, or something far more meaningful – curiosity, opportunity, and the belief someone places in us?

At ten, I discovered a drawer full of forgotten robotics parts. What began as curiosity grew into a journey through robotics, challenges, finding my voice, and eventually inspiring the next generation. Vihana Desai is a Grade 11 student at Daly College, Indore, who uses science and technology to solve real problems in her community. She has represented India twice at the FIRST Robotics World Championship in Houston with Team Sigma 9692, winning multiple awards in consecutive years, and is the first individual from Madhya Pradesh to take part in FIRST Robotics. She created TelCheck, a portable device that measures the quality of cooking oil, which earned her the internationally recognized CREST Gold Award. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more a
title: The Drawer I Never Closed | Vihana Desai | TEDxDaly College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What do we inherit from the generations before us? A business, a name, or something less tangible—the stories, experiences, and passions that shape who we become?

And what shapes the stories we tell? Sometimes, it begins with the stories we grew up hearing.

In this talk, filmmaker and entrepreneur Devesh Dutt traces his family’s journey from cinema halls and film distribution in pre-Partition India to his own childhood surrounded by films. Though he didn’t inherit the family business, he inherited its stories, its spirit, and a love for cinema.

Through stories of family, ambition, loss, and reinvention, he reflects on how the stories we inherit shape the stories we tell—and the people we become.

Devesh Dutt is a film director, writer, and entrepreneur with over 20 years of experience across advertising and filmmaking. He is the Director of Liberty Pictures, an award-winning production house, and the filmmaker behind the award-winning short films *The Perspective* and *The Virus*.
title: Stories We Inherit, Stories We Tell | Devesh Dutt | TEDxDaly College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: A TED veteran and 15-time TEDx speaker, foreign policy expert Siddharth Rajhans brings another instalment in his series on India’s strategic foreign policy — exploring the recently concluded BRICS Summit of September 2026 and its implications for the emerging world order. From the iconic photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to the diplomatic dialogue bringing these global powers to the same table, this talk examines India’s growing role in shaping a changing world order. The talk explores: • BRICS 2026 and its geopolitical significance. • India’s evolving engagement with China and Russia • The emerging multipolar world order. • India’s Vishwa Bandhu approach and leadership of the Global South. Is India merely witnessing the reshaping of the world order, or is it helping write its next chapter? This is Bharat Bhagya Vidhata. This is India’s moment. #TEDx #BRICS2026 #SiddharthRajhans #BharatBhagyaVidhata #India
title: BRICS 2026: Bharat Bhagya Vidhata | Siddhart Rajhans | TEDxDaly College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Vidyuth Sunder, an introverted student, shares how stepping outside his comfort zone transformed his middle school experience. Overwhelmed by a new and unfamiliar social environment, his founded a mythology club to build meaningful connections. Initially attended by just three friends, the club grew through creative strategies inspired by observing other student organizations, including candy, games, and school announcements. Eventually, attendance reached 30 students per meeting, turning a small initiative into a thriving community. Through this experience, he discovered that building connections begins with understanding others.  7th grade student at University Preparatory Academy, San Jose, CA. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Find Your Passion⫸Make Friends | Vidyuth Sunder | TEDxUPA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
白安是一位用音樂書寫人生的創作歌手。自發行首張專輯《麥田捕手》以來，她以清新的聲線與獨特的電子民謠風格受到關注，其中〈是什麼讓我遇見這樣的你〉更在網路上累積了破億觀看。多年來，她持續創作，用音樂記錄情感、成長與生活中的細微瞬間。在今天的分享中，她將帶我們走進創作的世界，看看一段旋律如何成為人生故事的一部分。 白安出生於台灣，她是新世代創作女聲 🎤，以氣質清新、唱腔獨特聞名，擅長電子民謠與輕盈電子聲響的音樂風格。
2012 年發行首張專輯《麥田捕手》，其中〈是什麼讓我遇見這樣的你〉MV 在 YouTube 累積破億觀看次數 💫。此後，她陸續推出全創作專輯《接下來是什麼》、《1990s》、《44天》、《沒有人寫歌給你過吧》及《星期八》，持續在華語樂壇拓展屬於自己的音樂版圖 ✨。
白安的作品風格獨樹一格，既展現創作才華，也在每一次發行中探索新的音樂可能。 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: 未完待續 To Be Continued: 我們為什麼那麼需要意義？ | 白安  | TEDxTaipei Fuhsing Private School

author: TEDx Talks
description: What does it mean to be Chamorrita? In a matriarchal culture where land and lineage pass through women, it means inheriting the decisions, the duty, and the weight of holding everyone together. Eva spent years certain she had failed that inheritance. She traces the word back to its root, haga', which means both blood and daughter, and redefines what that inheritance is: not a struggle to endure, but the power to decide what comes next. Eva Aguon Cruz, known as Eva Chamorrita, is a Chamoru artist, educator and advocate born and raised on Guåhan. Her work engages and empowers her people through cultural elevation and revitalization, with the aim of restoring Indigenous lands and lifeways. She serves as Executive Director of the Hagåtña Restoration and Redevelopment Authority. She has presented on Chamoru identity, decolonization and Pacific women's genealogies at conferences in Australia, Germany, Hawai'i, New Zealand, Palau and across the Marianas. This talk was given at a TEDx event u
title: Living My Ancestors’ Dream | Eva Aguon Cruz | TEDxTumon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In 2011, David Porter suddenly experienced the world as though he were listening underwater. After months of misdiagnoses, he learned he had tinnitus: relentless buzzing, clicking, and ringing with no moments of silence. In 2017, an audiologist helped him obtain insurance approval for a cochlear implant, making him the 10th US citizen to qualify. When wearing it, his tinnitus disappears, giving him 45 minutes of peace when removed.

He argues that, with the growing amount of noise in the world, 45 minutes of silence and reflection could help people rediscover their shared humanity, diminish divisions, and build a society with greater compassion and less hate. Forty-five minutes is a great place to start. As the school Director of University Preparatory Academy, San Jose, CA, David Porter is the 10th US citizen to qualify for the cochlear implant because of his tinnitus. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community
title: Taking a Break: The Uncomfortable Sound of Silence | David Porter | TEDxUPA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk will explore what it means to be a first-generation Hispanic student trying to build a path that nobody in the speaker's immediate family has taken before. At UPA, Belen has access to opportunities that can shape my future, however, figuring out how to use those opportunities can  feel like trying to navigate without a map, or going on a hike without an end goal. The central idea of the talk is that when there is no roadmap, you can learn to draw one yourself. The goal for this is to communicate that just because you're the first in your family to do something does not mean that you have to hold back from asking for help. 12th Grade first-generation Hispanic student at University Preparatory Academy, San Jose, CA. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: First Generation, Not First to Ask For Help | Belen Hernandez Ruiz | TEDxUPA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When we were little we were told we could do anything we set our minds to, but as
we grew older, something changed, we were now told to be realistic and not be overconfident with ourselves. However, some of the most successful people did not leave this mental approach behind. Numerous pro Olympic-level athletes hold an enormous amount of delusion while competing. This crucial unrealistic understanding of their own skills is what separates them from others. The talk will be about the power of your own mind and how deceiving yourself will make you more successful. It will include personal experiences of the speaker attempting to navigate and find that lost mindset throughout his competitive archery career. With his career giving him insight and an opportunity to talk with many Olympic and pro athletes, all mentioned their struggles with training their mind. It is not as easy as just saying “I am the best”, but it's really believing the power of confidence that comes from recognizing the
title: The Delusion of Being Delusional | Dylan Sim | TEDxUPA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
You can literally become whoever you want to be. This talk is centered on comparing life to a movie and how to become and design your own main character. (Basically, how to create your own character and how to become them).

You can’t “direct” what happens, but you can write your own character and how they would handle what happens. Movies always have plot twists, and the way the main character handles them is what makes the ending meaningful (and she'll compare them to life’s obstacles in the talk). 10th Grade Student at University Preparatory Academy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How Do You Put On Your Shoes? | Addison Nguyen | TEDxUPA Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Experience the rich sounds of Nepal’s musical heritage through this special instrumental performance by Lakshya Band at TEDxChipledhunga.

A traditional folk instrumental band from Pokhara, Lakshya Band brings together the soulful sounds of traditional Nepali instruments with the energy of contemporary musical expression. Their performance celebrates the diversity of Nepal’s musical traditions, taking audiences on a journey through familiar folk melodies, festive rhythms, and timeless compositions.

From the traditional Malshree Dhun, associated with the celebration of Dashain, to the lively rhythms of Kirati Rai folk music, the band brings together musical traditions from different parts of Nepal. Their performance also features instrumental interpretations of contemporary Nepali songs, connecting generations through the universal language of music.

Through their unique sound and energetic performance, Lakshya Band reminds us that our musical heritage is not just something to rememb
title: Echoes of Nepal: A Traditional Folk Performance | Lakshya Band | TEDxChipledhunga

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As families become increasingly spread across cities and countries, caring for ageing parents from a distance has become an emotional and logistical challenge. While technology has transformed healthcare, the everyday coordination of eldercare remains fragmented, leaving families struggling to stay informed and connected.

AI Chief Caregiver introduces a new perspective on eldercare by using Artificial Intelligence as a coordination and visibility layer that brings together caregiver updates, medical reports, medication records, and daily wellness check-ins into one unified platform.

The talk explores how AI can bridge the distance between ageing parents and their children, transforming scattered information into meaningful insights and timely alerts, while keeping human care, empathy, and decision-making at the centre.

It challenges the conventional approach to eldercare and presents a future where technology does not replace caregivers but empowers families to care better, stay co
title: AI Chief Caregiver Redefining Future of Remote Eldercare | Aaratrika Dwivedi | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the dreams that seem impossible today are simply ideas waiting for their time?

In this inspiring talk, Shivaganesh Gaddam, Founder of ZENi5, challenges the belief that extraordinary achievements require age, wealth, or exceptional privilege. Drawing from his entrepreneurial journey towards building India's first student bank, he shares how an ambitious vision can be transformed into reality through perseverance, consistency, and small, deliberate steps.

From facing scepticism and building trust among students and parents to securing investor confidence and earning recognition through a $100,000 grant and Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia, Shivaganesh reveals the realities behind pursuing a seemingly impossible dream.

The talk encourages young minds to rethink limitations, embrace calculated risks, and recognise that innovation is not about waiting for the perfect time but having the courage to begin.

Because sometimes, a dream isn't too big. You're just early. CA Aspirant with exten
title: Your Dream Isn’t Too Big. You’re Just Early. | Shivaganesh Gaddam | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In an era where technology is transforming economies, redefining human roles, and reshaping the way we live and work, one question becomes increasingly important: Are we using data, or have we ourselves become the data?

In this thought-provoking talk, Dr. Rajendra N. Paramanik explores the evolving relationship between individuals, technology, and the modern economy. Drawing connections between economics, human behaviour, creativity, and culture, he introduces the three defining dimensions of the contemporary economy: Commerce, Creativity, and Culture.

The talk challenges audiences to rethink what they learn, how they make economic decisions, and how they prepare for a rapidly changing future. From financial awareness and communication to creative thinking and generational value systems, it highlights the importance of balancing technological advancement with distinctly human qualities.

Ultimately, the talk invites us to question conventional ideas of success and progress and disco
title: Rethinking Our Place in an AI-Driven Economy | Dr. Rajendra N. Paramanik | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Can a child save a life? What if the knowledge and confidence to respond to a medical emergency could begin right inside a classroom?

In this powerful and thought-provoking talk, Dr. Parag Shankarrao Dekate challenges the conventional boundaries of school education by highlighting the importance of integrating health awareness, first aid, and life-saving skills into children's learning journeys.

Drawing from a personal experience that transformed his perspective on healthcare, he shares how a simple question evolved into a larger mission to empower teachers, school staff, and children with essential emergency response skills. From CPR and Basic Life Support to preventive healthcare, mental well-being, and nurturing future medical professionals, he explores how schools can become the foundation of a healthier and safer society.

The talk also highlights the importance of supporting teachers' health, extending healthcare access to families, and reaching children who need critical medi
title: What If the Next Lifesaver Is a Child? | Dr. Parag Shankarrao Dekate | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We carefully monitor the food we eat, the water we drink, and the air we breathe. But how often do we think about the sounds we are exposed to every single day?

In this thought-provoking talk, the speaker explores the often-overlooked impact of acoustic pollution on our concentration, emotional well-being, patience, and ability to learn. From traffic noise and mechanical hums to overcrowded classrooms and constant digital notifications, the talk uncovers how our everyday sound environments can influence the way we think, feel, and perform.

Challenging the tendency to label students as distracted, impatient, or lacking discipline, the speaker invites us to look beyond individual behaviour and recognise the role our surroundings play in shaping human potential.

The talk introduces practical ways to redesign our acoustic environments through quiet zones, nature-inspired classroom spaces, and intentional periods of silence, encouraging schools, families, and communities to make mindful
title: The Sound of Silence – Redesigning Our Acoustic Reality | Uttara Yarlagadda | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the future of agriculture could be transformed by a young mind with a passion for robotics and artificial intelligence?

In this inspiring talk, Kaashyap explores how technology can address some of the everyday challenges faced by farmers, from inefficient water management and crop diseases to the limitations of accessing modern agricultural solutions in rural areas.

Drawing attention to the realities of Indian farming, the talk challenges the idea that technological innovation must always depend on expensive equipment or constant internet connectivity. Instead, it introduces the possibilities of combining the Internet of Things (IoT), offline artificial intelligence, affordable sensors, and solar-powered automation to create practical solutions that work directly in the fields.

Through examples such as automated irrigation systems, soil-moisture monitoring, and offline crop disease detection, Kaashyap demonstrates how young innovators can use their curiosity, creativity, an
title: Silent fields-offline AI and IoT redesign farming | Kaashyap Sri Nandan kathi | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the greatest limitation a person faces is not a lack of ability, but the lack of an opportunity to discover it?

In this inspiring and reflective talk, the speaker challenges the way we measure success and perceive individual potential. Through relatable examples, the talk explores how academic struggles, early failures, social judgments, and preconceived expectations can lead people to underestimate themselves and their abilities.

It also sheds light on the invisible barriers that prevent individuals from pursuing their dreams, including financial limitations, family expectations, and societal pressures. What may appear to be a lack of ambition or capability could simply be an unexplored talent waiting for the right opportunity.

The talk invites parents, teachers, and communities to rethink how they encourage young minds, replacing labels with possibilities and limitations with opportunities for exploration. It emphasises the importance of creating an environment where indi
title: The Potential We Fail to See | Gayatri Boyapati | TEDxWorld One School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the true value of your business wasn't measured by the money you made, but by the people you impacted and the lives you transformed?

In this inspiring TEDx Talk, the speaker explores The Human Ledger—an invisible account of trust earned, relationships nurtured, people empowered, and lives transformed through entrepreneurship and leadership.

Rooted in a modest farming background, his entrepreneurial journey reflects how trust, mentorship, meaningful partnerships, and human connections can become far more valuable than financial capital.

From choosing business partners to building a team, every decision leaves a mark on the Human Ledger. This philosophy was truly tested when a devastating fire destroyed his company's physical infrastructure. Faced with rebuilding everything, he realised that his greatest assets were not buildings or machinery, but his people, their dignity, and their trust.

This talk offers a fresh perspective on entrepreneurship, people-first leadership, an
title: The Human Ledger: The Balance Sheet That Truly Counts | Kirit Joshi | TEDxIPEC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We celebrate people who give endlessly, put others first, and sacrifice their own needs for the greater good. But what happens when the very behaviors we praise begin to destroy the people practicing them?
In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Dr. Shola Ezeokoli challenges the cultural glorification of self-sacrifice and explores how unchecked altruism can become a socially rewarded form of self-abandonment.
Drawing from personal experiences, compelling stories, and her work with high-achieving professionals, she examines how our desire to be good, helpful, and dependable can quietly erode our health, identity, relationships, and sense of personal agency.
She introduces the counterintuitive power of strategic inaction, healthy boundaries, and psychological sovereignty, challenging audiences to recognize that genuine compassion must include the person giving it.
The central message is simple but provocative: Doing good should never require destroying yourself in the process.
 Dr. Shola
title: The self destruction of altruism | Dr. Shola Ezeokoli | TEDxVero Beach

author: TEDx Talks
description:
物理学で革命的な発見が起こるとき、何が起きているのか。相対性理論の成立過程を例に語ります。「純音」の中に潜む「揺らぎ」に目を向けることで見えてくるのは、物理学にとどまらない、私たちの世界の捉え方への新たな示唆です。

What happens when revolutionary discoveries are made in physics? Using the development of the theory of relativity as an example, this talk explores the process behind such breakthroughs. By turning our attention to the “fluctuations” hidden within a “pure tone”, we can uncover new insights not only into physics but also into how we perceive and understand the world around us. Professor at the University of California, Berkeley. After earning both a bachelor’s degree and a Ph.D. from the University of Tokyo, he pursued his research career primarily in the United States. He specializes in theoretical physics, with research interests including particle physics, cosmology, and quantum gravity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: 小さなゆらぎから生まれる、新しい世界  A New World Born From A Small Fluctuation | Yasunori Nomura | TEDxUTokyoSalon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Per anni Marisandra Lizzi ha creduto nel potere di Internet di cambiare il mondo. Poi, qualcosa ha iniziato a incrinarsi. Prima una sensazione difficile da spiegare, poi una domanda impossibile da ignorare.
Dall'entusiasmo per la rivoluzione digitale alla collaborazione con Amazon, Marisandra racconta il percorso che l'ha portata a mettere in discussione il proprio lavoro, i propri valori e il significato stesso del successo.
Rompendo il tabù di rinunciare a ciò che abbiamo costruito, ci invita a riflettere sui compromessi che accettiamo, sui segnali che scegliamo di non ascoltare e sul coraggio necessario per ritrovare coerenza con noi stessi.
#lavorotossico #cambiarevita #crisiprofessionale #ascoltareilcorpo #coraggiodicambiare
 Giornalista e imprenditrice, ha fondato Mirandola Comunicazione nel 2002. Dopo aver accompagnato per diciotto anni la comunicazione di Amazon in Italia, ha scelto di interrompere la collaborazione e ripensare il proprio lavoro, mettendo al centro l’etica, la
title: Il corpo sa quello che la mente nasconde | Marisandra Lizzi | TEDxReggio Emilia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Viviamo in una società ossessionata dalla bellezza, dall'apparenza e dalla perfezione, dove essere considerati brutti può diventare motivo di giudizio ed esclusione. Renato Fontana rompe il tabù della bruttezza e mette in discussione i canoni estetici che condizionano il modo in cui guardiamo noi stessi e gli altri.
Attraverso l'arte, la cultura e la comunicazione, ci invita a superare la contrapposizione tra bello e brutto, per riscoprire il valore dell'imperfezione e la libertà di essere ciò che siamo.
#bruttezza #standarddibellezza #accettazionedisé #bodyshaming #autostima #pregiudiziestetici
 Professionista della comunicazione d’avanguardia, riconosciuto per la capacità di coniugare in modo originale creatività, arte e cultura in progetti dalla forte componente innovativa. Esperto di linguaggi giovanili e trend culturali. Vanta 35 anni di esperienza sul campo, maturata prima in agenzie internazionali di comunicazione e con importanti clienti, sia in ambito privato che pubblico/ist
title: Il tabù della bruttezza: liberi dai canoni estetici | Renato Fontana | TEDxReggio Emilia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dodici ore di lavoro nei campi per venti euro. Soumaila parte dalla propria esperienza di bracciante agricolo per raccontare ciò che spesso rimane invisibile dietro i prodotti che acquistiamo: lo sfruttamento, il caporalato e le condizioni di vita di chi lavora nella filiera agricola.
In una società che riconosce a ogni persona pari dignità, perché accettiamo di non vedere chi paga davvero il prezzo di ciò che compriamo? Rompendo il tabù del silenzio e dell'ipocrisia, Soumaila propone una maggiore trasparenza sulle condizioni di lavoro e sulle retribuzioni lungo la filiera, per restituire alle persone un valore che non può essere misurato dal prezzo di un prodotto.
#caporalato #sfruttamentolavorativo #schiavitùmoderna #dirittideilavoratori  #sfruttamentobracciantiagricoli
 Soumaila Diawara, nato a Bamako nel 1988, è scrittore, giornalista, attivista per i diritti umani e rifugiato politico originario del Mali. Laureato in Scienze Giuridiche, con specializzazione in diritto privato int
title: Dignità del lavoro: cosa e chi c’è dietro a ciò che compriamo | Soumaïla Diawara | TEDxReggio Emilia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Cosa succede quando il pregiudizio diventa un ostacolo alla conoscenza scientifica?
Partendo da argomenti che spesso suscitano imbarazzo, come l'infertilità maschile e la cannabis, la biologa molecolare Fiorenza ci accompagna alla scoperta del sistema endocannabinoide, un complesso sistema di regolazione presente nel nostro organismo, coinvolto in numerosi processi fisiologici, dalla riproduzione alla risposta allo stress.
Attraverso la propria esperienza di ricerca e le storie di scienziati che hanno sfidato paure e pregiudizi, Fiorenza ci invita a rompere i tabù che circondano il nostro corpo e la scienza. Perché la curiosità, accompagnata dal rigore scientifico, può aprire la strada a scoperte capaci di migliorare la vita delle persone.
